precepts.text: Christ spake openly to the world, in the synagogue and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; the world he spoke to was Israel.
precepts.point: That settles 1 John 2:2 for the Christians who run to it. John was a Jew of the southern kingdom, so our sins means the southern kingdom; and not for ours only but also for the sins of the whole world means all twelve tribes, the whole world of Israel. Alongside Isaiah 45:17 and John 18:20, Wisdom of Solomon 18:24 is the precept that shows who the whole world is.

note.label: Exodus 28: Holy Garments for Glory and for Beauty

precepts.why:
“I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.” The world Christ spoke openly to was the synagogue and the temple, where the Jews always resort: the world he spoke to was Israel.

That is the same whole world of the breastplate, the four rows of stones with the names of the twelve tribes, and the same whole world whose sins Christ is the propitiation for in 1 John 2:2. With Isaiah 45:17 and Wisdom of Solomon 18:24, it shows who the whole world is: the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.text: I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort.
precepts.point: John's own gospel names who the world is: the one he was made manifest to, the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the one he taught openly in the synagogue and the temple.

note.label: John 3: Nicodemus, the Serpent Lifted Up, and Who the World Is

precepts.why:
“Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing.”

He spake openly to the world, and then he says where: in the synagogue and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort. The world he taught openly was the Jews in the synagogue and the temple. Put it with the one he was made manifest to and the one the Pharisees said was gone after him, and the world God so loved is named plainly in John's own gospel.

precepts.text: Annas was father-in-law to Caiaphas, who was the high priest that same year, so they were tied by marriage.
precepts.point: Caiaphas prophesied that one man should die for the people, speaking not of himself but from the prophecies he knew in Isaiah 53 and the Psalms. That nation he must die for is Israel, and "not for that nation only" means Christ would also gather the children of God scattered abroad, the twelve tribes, not the Gentiles the Christians claim.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
When Christ was taken they “led him away to Annas first; for he was father in law to Caiaphas, which was the high priest that same year.”

Annas and Caiaphas were tied by marriage, the kindred of the high priest gathered at Jerusalem. These were the very persons who procured the death of Christ, and now the apostles stand before them.
